name: Ashéninka Perené
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: La acentuación de «jaká» (y de los otros deícticos adverbiales de lugar derivados de la protoestructura <ja>) contraviene las reglas de acentuación en asháninka, donde generalmente estas son graves. Sin embargo, existe una tendencia de la dependencia de la acentuación de la sonoridad del núcleo silábico, por lo que se considera que la escala de sonoridad de las vocales en asháninka es la siguiente: [a] > [e] > [o] > [i]. Además, se considera fonémico por lo que permite diferenciar significados. Además, el alargamiento puede ser usado como una estrategia discursiva para enfatizar la naturaleza del evento (Mihas, 2010: 50, 75).
new_statements.translation: The stress of «jaká» (and of the other adverbial place deictics derived from the proto-structure <ja>) goes against the stress rules of Asháninka, where [words] are generally paroxytone [stressed on the penultimate syllable]. However, there is a tendency for stress to depend on the sonority of the syllabic nucleus, so the vowel sonority scale of Asháninka is taken to be [a] > [e] > [o] > [i]. Moreover, it [vowel length] is considered phonemic since it distinguishes meanings; and lengthening can be used as a discourse strategy to emphasize the nature of the event (Mihas 2010: 50, 75).

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: QUOTE CHECK:, printed p. 112 = PDF p. 116 (extracted text): the whole passage from "La acentuación de «jaká»..." to "... (Mihas, 2010: 50, 75)." is there word for word, in §5.4.1 "El deíctico adverbial de lugar «jaká»". Elsewhere Solari only has an orthographic aside (p. 77) on the Spanish accent of the ethnonym; no phonology section. IDENTITY: Solari's data are from three Chanchamayo (Junín) communities (Alto Incariado, Zotziki Cerro Picaflor,...) collected 2014-2018, explicitly "el dialecto ashéninka del Alto Perené" (pp. 25-27, fn. 2-3) = Upper Perené = ashe1272 (prq); Mihas 2015 snippet: "Alto Perené reflects the speech communities of the Upper Perené valley". Pedrós 2023 §2.5 (LOT 640,…
new_statements.rule_in_words: As reported second-hand: stress in Alto Perené Ashéninka is generally on the penultimate syllable, with a tendency for stress to be attracted by more sonorous nuclei (a > e > o > i); the final-stressed place deictics jaká, jará, jantá, jantó are exceptions. The primary description (Mihas 2015: 56-58; Mihas 2010: 50, 75) was not seen; Pedrós 2023: 81 states that Mihas' Alto Perené patterns are 'quite different' from the Ucayali-Pajonal ones 'above all in disyllabic words', so the penultimate default should be treated as unverified. Related Kampan varieties (Pichis, Apurucayali, Ucayali-Pajonal, Nanti) are described as weight-/quality-sensitive iambic systems with final extrametricality, so a weight-sensitive reading is plausible for the primary source.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said for Alto Perené. (Pedrós 2023 §2.5 reports secondary stresses on enclitics and in longer words for Ucayali-Pajonal only.)
new_statements.exceptions: Final-stressed place deictics jaká/jará/jantá/jantó (Solari 2020: 112); a vowel-sonority tendency a > e > o > i overriding the default.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level remark about isolated deictic adverbs in a syntax/semantics thesis; no citation-form vs phrase discussion. Vowel length is separately noted as phonemic.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted source (Solari 2020) calls the variety 'asháninka del Alto Perené' (data from Perené-valley communities, Chanchamayo, Junín) — this is the Alto/Upper Perené variety described by Mihas, i.e. ashe1272 (ISO prq), not Tambo-Ene Asháninka (cni). Pedrós 2023 (LOT 640), the only open grammar with a full stress section, describes Ucayali-Pajonal Ashéninka (Gran Pajonal/Ucayali; ISO cjo/cpb group), a different Glottolog languoid; its §2.5 must not be read as an ashe1272 description — it only points to Mihas 2015: 56-58 for Alto Perené and says the Alto Perené patterns differ from its own.

sources.citation: Pedrós, Toni. 2023. A grammar of Ashéninka (Ucayali-Pajonal). LOT Dissertation Series 640. Amsterdam: LOT. DOI 10.48273/lot0640. Section 2.5 'Stress', pp. 81-91.
sources.note: Describes UCAYALI-PAJONAL Ashéninka (not ashe1272): stress non-phonemic, tendency-based; di-/trisyllables penult, tetrasyllables antepenult, bimoraic syllables strongest attractors, iambic feet in longer words. On p. 81 it says: 'Payne, Payne & Sánchez (1982:185-95) describe the stress patterns for Apurucayali and Mihas (2015a:56-58) for Alto Perené... Regarding Mihas' patterns, they are quite different from mine, above all in disyllabic words.' So the Alto Perené stress description is Mihas 2015: 56-58; content not given.

sources.citation: Martel Paredes, Víctor Arturo. 2012. La reduplicación verbal en el ashaninka del alto Perené desde la teoría de la optimalidad. Tesis de magíster, PUCP, Lima. hdl 20.500.12404/1522.
sources.note: pp. 76-78 restate J. Payne (1991) rules for 'asheninka' (heavy VV syllables attract primary stress, final syllable extrametrical, binary L-to-R right-headed feet, clash resolution); uses a STRESS constraint ('los núcleos vocálicos complejos atraen... acento') for Alto Perené reduplication but gives no independent Alto Perené stress rule.
